title: Reference workbook leaves a material subtotal omission unrepaired
evidence: The task requires correcting formula errors and omissions so subtotals and roll-ups calculate properly, but the reference workbook retains ENA!M62 as the constant 0. Its component plan margins M57:M61 are 0, 12.9, 0, 0 and 4, totaling 16.9. Other plan columns in row 62 correctly sum rows 57–61. Consequently, the reference's Total Commercial margin M76 is understated by 16.9, and its final margin M139 of 2211.8 less capital charges of 0 and expenses of 668.2 produces EBIT of 1543.6, inconsistent with Q139's 1560.5. The reference changes 28 shifted EBIT formulas but does not repair this omission. Because the rubric uses binary logical-equivalence grading and checks modifications against the reference, this incomplete reference can penalize a competent agent that restores the missing subtotal, or credit an audit that leaves the roll-ups unreconciled.
confirmation: Same verified defect: the GT keeps ENA!M62=0 although M57:M61=16.9 and the rest of row 62 uses SUM, so M139 (2211.8) less expenses (668.2) does not reconcile to Q139 (1560.5).
fix: gt_133_ref_0.xlsx ENA!M62: hardcoded 0 -> =SUM(M57:M61) (16.9), matching N62:Q62. Cached values of its roll-ups updated in place (formulas kept): M76 2205 -> 2221.9, M139 2211.8 -> 2228.7, so M139-N139-O139 now reconciles to Q139 1560.5. A LibreOffice recalculation of the patched GT confirms these are the only 3 cells that change. The 28 original Q95:Q128 fixes are untouched.

title: Ground truth workbook fails to fix the omitted =SUM(M57:M61) subtotal formula in ENA!M62 and its cascading roll-ups (M76, M139)
evidence: The task prompt instructs the agent: "Audit the consolidated 2002 plan workbook and correct the formula errors and omissions so the subtotals and roll-ups calculate properly." In `133_src_0.xlsx` on the `ENA` sheet, Row 62 (`  Upstream Products`) is the subtotal row for Rows 57:61 (`Upstream Executive` through `Producer E-Commerce`, where `M58=12.9` and `M61=4`). In the 2002 Plan block (columns M:Q), `N62` (`=SUM(N57:N61)`), `O62` (`=SUM(O57:O61)` = 2.4), `P62` (`=SUM(P57:P61)` = 0), and `Q62` (`=SUM(Q57:Q61)` = 14.5) all contain `=SUM(...)` subtotal formulas, whereas `M62` (2002 Plan Margin) has a hardcoded `0` instead of `=SUM(M57:M61)` (which equals 16.9). Because `M62` is hardcoded as `0` while `Q62` sums the row-level EBITs (`14.5 = 16.9 - 2.4`), the 2002 Plan subtotals and roll-ups do not reconcile horizontally (`M - N - O - P != Q` by 16.9) at Row 62 (`M62=0` vs `Q62=14.5`), Row 76 `Total Commercial ` (`M76=2205` vs `2221.9`, so `M76-N76-O76=1933.4 != Q76=1950.3`), and Row 139 `EBIT` (`M139=2211.8` vs `2228.7`, so `M139-N139-O139=1543.6 != Q139=1560.5`). Furthermore, the prompt explicitly asks to correct "formula errors and omissions so the subtotals and roll-ups calculate properly", yet the ground-truth workbook (`gt_133_ref_0.xlsx`) leaves `ENA!M62=0` unchanged (`M76=2205`, `M139=2211.8`) and only changes 28 row-level EBIT formulas in `ENA!Q95:Q108, Q111:Q115, Q120:Q128` from `=N{r}-O{r}-P{r}` to `=M{r}-N{r}-O{r}` (where both `M` and `P` are 0 in all 28 rows, so zero values or subtotals change in the GT). Under the `grader_guidance` Evaluation Criteria ("2. Data Accuracy: For cells involved in the instruction, are the model's values/text/formulas logically equivalent to the reference answer..." and "3. Reasonableness of Changes: ... The model should not make modifications not mentioned in the instruction"), a competent agent that fixes the obvious `M62` subtotal omission (`=SUM(M57:M61)`) will have different formulas and values in `M62`, `M76`, and `M139` than the reference answer and risk failing `correctness` / `over_edit_avoidance` (which maps to a binary 0/1 overall score).
confirmation: ENA!M62 is a hardcoded 0 while N62:Q62 are =SUM(row57:61) and M57:M61 total 16.9 (M58=12.9, M61=4). gt_133_ref_0.xlsx leaves M62 unchanged (only Q95:Q128 differ), so an agent that fixes this obvious subtotal omission diverges from the reference on M62, M76 and M139.
fix: gt_133_ref_0.xlsx ENA!M62: hardcoded 0 -> =SUM(M57:M61) (16.9), matching N62:Q62. Cached values of its roll-ups updated in place (formulas kept): M76 2205 -> 2221.9, M139 2211.8 -> 2228.7, so M139-N139-O139 now reconciles to Q139 1560.5. A LibreOffice recalculation of the patched GT confirms these are the only 3 cells that change. The 28 original Q95:Q128 fixes are untouched.

title: Reference answer leaves a broken roll-up in place (ENA row 62 'Upstream Products'), so an agent that does what the prompt asks gets marked wrong
evidence: The prompt asks the agent to 'correct the formula errors and omissions so the subtotals and roll-ups calculate properly.' On the ENA sheet, row 62 is a subtotal. H62:K62, N62:Q62 and S62:U62 are all =SUM(row57:row61). But M62 (2002 Plan Margin) is a hardcoded 0, while M57:M61 add up to 16.9 (M58=12.9, M61=4). Its own EBIT cell Q62=SUM(Q57:Q61) gives 14.5. So on row 62, Margin 0 − Capital 0 − Direct 2.4 does not equal EBIT 14.5. The error carries up: Total Commercial M76 is understated by 16.9, and so are EBIT-row M139 and M131-linked totals, while Q76/Q139 include the 14.5. The rendered page shows it: Upstream Products, 2002 Plan Margin '-' next to EBIT '14.5'. The same row in the 2001 Forecast is also hardcoded (C62=21, D62=1.5, E62=4.7) while C57:E61 are all 0, which breaks the SUM pattern used in H62. The GT (gt_133_ref_0.xlsx) changes none of these cells. A cell-by-cell diff of source vs GT shows the only edits are ENA Q95:Q128. The grader is binary: a 0/1 score that requires the output to be 'logically equivalent to the reference' and also checks 'over_edit_avoidance'. An agent that correctly sets M62 (and C62:E62) to SUMs will change M76/M139 values that the GT does not, and risks failing.
confirmation: Confirmed with a cell diff: only 28 cells in Q95:Q128 change in the GT, while the broken M62 subtotal (0 against components summing to 16.9) stays. A competent fix therefore differs from the binary-graded reference.
fix: gt_133_ref_0.xlsx ENA!M62: hardcoded 0 -> =SUM(M57:M61) (16.9), matching N62:Q62. Cached values of its roll-ups updated in place (formulas kept): M76 2205 -> 2221.9, M139 2211.8 -> 2228.7, so M139-N139-O139 now reconciles to Q139 1560.5. A LibreOffice recalculation of the patched GT confirms these are the only 3 cells that change. The 28 original Q95:Q128 fixes are untouched. grader_guidance.md: added after the first paragraph: 'On the ENA sheet, the 2001 Forecast cells C62:E62 are typed totals with no detail in rows 57 to 61, so accept either leaving them as they are or replacing them with SUM formulas.'
